transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-10 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Martinez (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Voxera Head of ML), Liam O'Neill (Platform Eng), Sophie Kramer (PM), Tom Rivers (DevOps)

[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for jumping on, I'm Avery from Redwood, AE on this account. Diego and Priya are with me on the product and kernel side. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Maya: Good, thanks. Busy sprint but excited to see the catalog stuff, we wanted to understand how to pick models that make sense for our voice-to-text and summarization pipelines.
[00:18] Liam: Yep we have a 1k qps window during business hours and it's pretty bursty, so cost is a big factor but latency SLA is 300 ms tail.
[00:28] Diego: Great, that's super helpful. We'll try to map demo artifacts back to that SLA. Quick agenda — catalog filters, decision matrix walkthrough, heatmap interpretation, and then compatibility matrix and kernel mapping. Then we'll leave time for scoping a short pilot. Sound good?
[00:40] Sophie: Sounds good.
[00:42] Tom: Yep.
[01:22] Avery: I'll start with the console — this is the model catalog. You can see we surface open models with a few curated columns: typical latency at 128 tokens, cost units, and a quality score derived from evals. Note that the quality score is relative to the workload we onboard.
[02:10] Avery: One thing we push is the decision matrix; you can apply filters for latency, cost per token, and kernel support. So for example if you filter for models with A100 optimized kernels and <200 ms median latency, you get this shortlist —
[02:30] (screen share stutters)
[02:35] Maya: Quick q — how accurate are the latency numbers? Are they from your hosted infra or synthetic?
[02:42] Priya: They're from our benchmark suite run across representative hardware. For hosted numbers we run on our fleet and normalize; for Dedicated they'd be measured on reserved pools but we provide guidance via kernel compatibility and perf curves. There is some variance based on sequence length and KV cache hits.
[03:10] Liam: When you say KV cache hits is that the same as K-V cash? (laughs)
[03:14] Diego: Yeah sometimes the transcript spells it K-V cash, but it's KV cache — basically key-value cache for transformer past keys to speed up streaming.
[03:22] Maya: Ok makes sense.
[04:05] Diego: Let's look at heatmaps — this one plots median latency on Y, cost per 1k tokens on X, color shows quality delta versus our baseline. You can see a cluster of smaller quantized models that are low-cost, low-latency but a slight drop in quality for summarization.
[04:35] Sophie: Is that color scale customizable? We have internal benchmarks that weight summary factuality higher than generic perplexity.
[04:42] Diego: Yes, you can upload your own eval results and re-weight the quality score; the catalog will recalc and re-rank models for your decision matrix.
[05:01] Maya: That re-ranking sounds key. Can you show how we'd pick two candidates for a pilot?
[05:08] Avery: Sure — step one, pick a shortlist by our decision matrix: 1) mid-sized 8-bit quantized model with dedicated kernel support, 2) a slightly larger low-latency model with good prefix KV hit ratio. We'll then run them A/B on your prompt set.
[05:30] (background voice - Speaker 1: yeah i can..)
[06:00] Liam: On the infra side, our cluster uses a mixture of T4s and a few A10s — we'd probably want to test on both. Does Redwood's kernel mapper handle different GPU types?
[06:12] Diego: Yes, the compatibility matrix shows supported kernels per model per GPU family. For example the 8-bit quant path uses optimized kernels on A10/A100; on T4 we use an alternate kernel with slightly higher latency. We also surface recommended batch sizes per GPU.
[06:35] Tom: Any special network considerations for Private deployment? We run in a VPC with strict egress rules.
[06:44] Priya: For Private we offer a customer-managed control plane and VPC peering. We can provide network diagrams and a list of ports. We'll attach the SOC2 and network docs after the call.
[07:10] Maya: Can we get a runbook for rolling back if latency degrades after a rollout?
[07:18] Avery: Absolutely — our rollouts support canary by percentage with automatic fallback to pinned model variants. We'll include the rollback playbook in the pilot proposal.
[08:00] Diego: Now diving deeper — here's the kernel compatibility matrix. Columns are models, rows are GPU types; cells show kernel name and recommended quantization. You can export this as CSV and share with infra teams.
[08:30] Sophie: That export will be useful for procurement. Is there a way to tie cost estimates to a specific kernel (like kernel X on A10 gives Y tokens/sec)?
[08:42] Diego: Yes, every kernel has a performance profile. The console multiplies tokens/sec by our compute cost to produce per-1k token cost estimates. Keep in mind those are estimates; we'll run a pilot to surface real numbers on your traffic shape.
[09:20] Maya: We have compliance questions — SSO, SAML, and KMS for keys?
[09:27] Priya: We support SAML SSO, RBAC roles, and KMS/HSM integrations for Private and Dedicated. For Hosted, we also provide customer-managed keys via a bring-your-own-KMS option. We'll share the security pack.
[10:00] (crosstalk)
[11:00] Avery: Shifting to Bench harness — Diego, can you show the benchmark harness config?
[11:06] Diego: Yup. This harness runs prompts with your seed set, measures percentiles (p50/p95/p99), tokenization behavior, and measures KV cache hit ratio. For streaming use cases we also measure end-to-end latency including network time.
[11:35] Liam: Network time will be big for us. Are you able to run the harness from our VPC?
[11:42] Diego: Yes, during a pilot we can either run inside your VPC in Private mode or run controlled runs where we send a representative traffic recorder to your infra. For initial tests we usually do a short Dedicated test with our ingress to be quicker.
[12:10] Maya: Can we control temperature and generation length for the pilot? We want to mimic our production configs.
[12:16] Avery: Yes you'll be able to pass in generation parameters and a full prompt set. Also we'll instrument to collect quality metrics — rouge/factuality/semantic similarity — whatever you want to upload.
[13:00] (long pause / someone types)
[14:05] Sophie: A question on pricing — if we hit sustained throughput, what's the delta between Hosted and Dedicated? ballpark numbers fine.
[14:15] Avery: Ballpark: Hosted is more flexible but higher per-token unit cost. Dedicated is lower unit cost at the expense of commit and sometimes multi-hour slot scheduling. We'll send a pricing table. Example: on a 1M token monthly volume, Dedicated can be ~30-45% cheaper depending on model mix and quantization.
[15:00] Maya: Are there any vendor lock-in concerns if we start on Hosted and then move to Dedicated/Private?
[15:08] Priya: No, the point of Redwood is a unified API and same model catalog. You can pin model versions and move routes between hosted and dedicated — we support automated reroutes and test/rollback. There are infra differences but no code changes in your app.
[16:30] Diego: Let's do a quick live filter. I'll set map to 'summarization' and weight quality toward factuality. Notice the catalog reorders and now suggests two open models: 'orca-lite-8q' and 'clarion-v2-6b-q4'.
[16:50] Maya: Clarion-v2 sounds familiar — did you run internal summarization tests?
[16:54] Diego: We did, on our evals clarion-v2 had good factuality but is slightly higher latency on T4s. That's why it's in the middle of the heatmap.
[17:30] Liam: For the pilot can we run clarion on A10s and orca-lite on T4s to see real-world differences?
[17:36] Diego: Yes, that's exactly the pilot we typically recommend.
[18:20] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[19:00] Avery: Let's talk success criteria — to be actionable we propose: p95 under 350 ms for 95% of requests, cost per 1k tokens under $X (we'll define), and summary factuality > 0.85 on your scored set. If all three met we consider the pilot successful.
[19:30] Maya: That gives us a good rubric.
[20:12] Diego: On instrumentation — we'll add tracing hooks and correlation IDs so you can tie model output back to request IDs in your logs. That helps debug regressions during rollouts.
[21:00] Tom: For the kernel check — would Diego need any special access to our GPUs?
[21:07] Diego: Ideally we get a small test set deployed inside a sandbox that mirrors your env. Otherwise we can run synthetic runs but kernel micro-behavior is best tested on the same driver and CUDA stack.
[22:00] Sophie: Timeframe for a pilot? We want results within two weeks ideally.
[22:08] Avery: We can run a lightweight 7–14 day pilot. Initial runs and data collection in 48 hours then a longer soak. We'll scope the exact runbook.
[23:00] (laughter)
[24:10] Liam: One more Q on model updates — if an open model upstream gets updated how do we handle drift?
[24:18] Priya: We version models in the catalog; by default we do not auto-upgrade you — you pin to a model digest and can opt into updates. We also provide eval diffing so you can see quality regressions between versions.
[25:45] Diego: I'll also point out our Optimize tab — it will suggest quantization and batch settings for your observed workload. It can recommend a fallback variant for times when Dedicated capacity is saturated.
[26:30] Maya: Nice. Is Optimize able to simulate cost savings?
[26:35] Diego: Yes, given a traffic shape it will show projected token cost and latency changes for different configs. We treat it as guidance and then validate with a pilot.
[27:00] Priya: Quick note — we sometimes recommend prefix caching for conversational summarization to reduce token consumption. That requires small prompt reorg.
[27:18] Sophie: That's doable, our product team can make that change for the pilot.
[28:00] Avery: Ok wrapping toward next steps — do we agree on a 2-model A/B pilot, initial 48h runs then longer soak, and Redwood supplies SOC2/network docs plus pricing by the dates we discussed?
[28:12] Maya: Yes.
[28:15] Tom: Yes.
[28:30] Liam: We'll get the prompt set and the traffic replay by Friday.
[29:00] Diego: Great. I'll outline the harness and test scripts.
[30:00] (typing noises)
[31:10] Maya: Two follow-ups — will you include worst-case failover behavior? We need to know what happens if Dedicated nodes are preempted.
[31:20] Priya: Failover: Canary to other region or fallback to hosted model variant. We can configure automatic fallback policies with routing rules and retry windows. We'll include a flow chart.
[32:10] Sophie: Also procurement wants a CSV export of kernel compatibility and per-1k token cost estimates.
[32:18] Avery: We'll attach that in the follow-up.
[33:00] (silence)
[34:25] Diego: One more technical note — when you look at the kernel cell it sometimes says 'fused-attn-v2' or 'attn-legacy' — fused is faster but only supported on newer drivers. We'll surface driver requirements on export.
[35:00] Liam: We'll check our CUDA and driver versions.
[36:00] Maya: Any known blockers for streaming audio->text->summarize pipeline? We're worried about tokenization splitting causing latency spikes.
[36:12] Diego: Tokenization can introduce edge cases; we recommend normalizing text and applying a pre-tokenization step that clips long prefixes and batches smaller windows to avoid p99 spikes. We'll show sample pre-tokenization scripts.
[37:00] Tom: Good, that helps.
[38:20] Sophie: How do you handle sensitive PII in request logs during the pilot?
[38:28] Priya: We redacting options and we can enable payload-level redaction plus ephemeral logs in Private deployments. For Hosted, we do not persist user contents beyond short retention without a contract. We'll include redaction options in the security pack.
[39:00] Maya: Perfect.
[40:00] Avery: Summarize — Redwood to: send SOC2 & network diagrams by 2026-09-12, pricing and Dedicated bullets by 2026-09-14, Diego to prepare harness and kernel CSV by 2026-09-14, Voxera to share prompt sets and traffic replay by 2026-09-11. Pilot window 7–14 days starting asap after artifact exchange.
[40:30] Maya: We'll aim to get prompts by Friday.
[41:00] Sophie: One last ask — could you include an example rollback timeline (like minutes to failover)? Procurement likes explicit SLAs.
[41:10] Avery: Yes we'll include an appendix with typical SLOs and expected failover times. For our Dedicated to hosted fallbacks it's usually under 2 minutes for routing failover, but we'll make sure we list conservative numbers.
[42:00] (closing notes)
[43:00] Liam: Thanks everyone, this was great and very actionable.
[43:05] Maya: Thanks, speak soon.
[43:10] Avery: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the packet and draft pilot plan.
[43:20] (meeting ends, people leave)

Notes on transcription: small mislabels, occasional background noise and truncated words, some technical terms spelled phonetically (K-V cash). Overall medium quality.
